item.title: Juventus remains keen to sign Inter Milan star for free
item.description: Juventus remains keen to sign Inter Milan star for free Hakan Calhanoglu has yet to sign a new contract with Inter Milan, raising the possibility that the Turkish midfielder could leave the club as a free agent at the end of the season. His contract situation has attracted interest from Juventus, who are reportedly keen to bring him to Turin . Inter are aware of the situation and are working to prevent him from leaving without receiving a transfer fee. The club still considers Calhanoglu one of its most important players and would prefer to keep him, but negotiations over a new agreement have so far failed to produce a breakthrough. The situation could become more complicated in January, when the midfielder will be able to discuss a potential move with other clubs. Having spent around a decade playing in Serie A, he may prefer to continue his career in Italy rather than move abroad. Juventus prepare to pursue Calhanoglu Juventus are reportedly monitoring his contract situation closely and see him as one of the most attractive midfield options available in the Italian top flight. The Bianconeri believe the Turkish international has the qualities required to improve their current squad and are prepared to make an effort to secure his services. They are also aware that Inter would strongly oppose losing such an important player to one of their domestic rivals. However, Calhanoglu has previously demonstrated that he is willing to change clubs within Milan, having joined Inter after leaving AC Milan. His previous move suggests that remaining in Milan is not necessarily his only consideration when deciding his future. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Inter face uncertainty over his future According to Calciomercato , Juventus consider Calhanoglu the right profile for their current squad and will continue working towards bringing him to Turin. For now, the midfielder appears to be waiting for Inter to improve their contract offer, but negotiations have not progressed as hoped. This leaves the club facing an increasingly difficult situation as the season continues. Inter will be determined to avoid losing him for nothing, particularly given his importance to the team. However, unless both parties reach an agreement, the possibility of his departure will remain. Juventus could therefore have an opportunity to sign an experienced midfielder without paying a transfer fee next summer. Much will depend on how the contract negotiations develop over the coming months and whether Calhanoglu decides that a new challenge in Turin is the right step for his career.

item.title: Scouting New York Jets defensive lineman Isaiahh Loudermilk
item.description: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - JUNE 10: Isaiahh Loudermilk #69 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during minicamp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on June 10, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets recently signed former Steelers defensive lineman Isaiahh Loudermilk to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 29-year old Loudermilk is listed at 6’7” and 293 pounds and was a fifth round pick out of Wisconsin in 2021. He has started seven games in his NFL career, with 63 tackles, six passes defensed and one sack. Background Loudermilk was a three-star high school recruit despite only having played 8-man football in a small town. He ended up going to Wisconsin, where he redshirted his first season in 2016, but then became a useful player over the next few years. In 2017, Loudermilk had six tackles in 11 games in a reserve role, adding 1.5 sacks and a pass defensed. He started the first six games of his career in 2018 and ended up with 15 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, three passes defensed and a sack in nine games. In 2019, he started all 14 games and had his most productive season with 24 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, five pass breakups and two forced fumbles. However, Loudermilk got all Big-10 recognition for the only time in his final season as he was named as a third-teamer by the media and an honorable mention by the coaches. In just six games during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, he had 13 tackles and two sacks. After not being invited to the scouting combine, Loudermilk played in the East-West Shrine Bowl and was eventually drafted by the Steelers in the fifth round of the 2021 draft. As a rookie, he started two games and ended up with 23 tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in 15 appearances. In 2022, Loudermilk started three times but had just seven tackles and a tackle for loss in 11 games overall. He played in 16 games in both 2023 and 2024 but did not start a game during that time. He ended up with 33 tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit over the two seasons. 2025 saw Loudermilk start the first two games, although he didn’t generate any statistics. An injury in the second game sidelined him for the rest of the season. He was almost ready to return for the postseason but wasn’t cleared in time. Loudermilk signed for the Vikings in the offseason but failed to make their roster and was eventually added to the Jets’ practice squad last month. item.title: Houston Astros hire New York Yankees' Brad Ausmus as manager
item.description: Brad Ausmus previously managed the Los Angeles Angels and Detroit Tigers. File Photo by John Angelillo/UPI Nov. 11 (UPI) -- The Houston Astros hired New York Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus as their manager, they announced Wednesday. Ausmus, who previously played for the Astros, has an overall record of 386-422 as an MLB manager. He led the Los Angeles Angels in 2019 and Detroit Tigers from 2014 to 2017. "I am very excited to be back in Houston," Ausmus said in a news release. "The Astros and the city of Houston have been a huge part of my life, and I'm thrilled to create a new chapter as the team's manager." The Astros announced in October that former manager Joe Espada will not return in 2027. He compiled a 256-229 regular-season record over the last three years, including an 81-81 mark in 2026. The Astros were 0-4 in the postseason under Espada, who was hired in 2024. "We are thrilled to welcome Brad back to the Astros organization," Astros general manager Randy Flores said. "Brad impressed us throughout the interview process, demonstrating the leadership, energy, and expertise critical to driving a winning culture both on and off the field." Ausmus, 57, spent 10 of his 18 seasons as a player with the Astros. The All-Star catcher was a three-time Gold Glove Award winner. He also played for the Los Angeles Dodgers, San Diego Padres and Detroit Tigers. Ausmus joined the Yankees' staff in 2024. He was a bench coach for the Oakland Athletics in 2022.

item.title: Kirk Cousins sends message to Fernando Mendoza after Raiders-Vikings trade
item.description: Kirk Cousins sends message to Fernando Mendoza after Raiders-Vikings trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Las Vegas Raiders will trot out a new quarterback during the second half of the 2026-27 NFL campaign. Despite insisting Kirk Cousins was off-limits in trade talks, the AFC West franchise shipped the four-time Pro Bowl signal caller to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick on Tuesday, allowing Fernando Mendoza to finish his rookie season as Las Vegas's No. 1 QB. Shortly after Cousins’ trade was announced, the Michigan State product sent a brief message to Mendoza as he navigates life as a starting NFL quarterback. “Go get em,” Cousins said on Instagram while tagging Mendoza. Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has appeared in three games with the Raiders this year as a backup, completing six of his eight passes for 48 yards. Given Cousins’ veteran presence and consistent production throughout his career, the Raiders felt inclined to give the former Washington Commanders QB the nod to begin the new season. To Cousins’ credit, his play validated Las Vegas’ mildly controversial QB decision, as he’s completed 202 passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, and eight interceptions on the 4-5 Raiders. That said, it’s clear Las Vegas is ready to begin a new era in early November, and it’s highly unlikely it’ll backfire in the end. item.title: Chiefs Reveal Significant Chris Jones Update Before Falcons Game
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs started off the season strong with a 5-0 record. Over their last three games, however, things have cooled off and they head into Week 10 action with a 6-2 record. Granted, that still has the Chiefs looking like a potential Super Bowl contender in the AFC. Patrick Mahomes and the offense have done enough to win football games and the defense has been solid as well. At the end of the day, this season could be the last run at another championship with the main core in place. Mahomes, Travis Kelce, and Chris Jones are still the unquestioned leaders in Kansas City. Jones may not receive the hype that Mahomes and Kelce do, but his presence is crucial to the Chiefs’ ability to win at a high level. That much can be seen even more following the announcement Kansas City made about Jones on Wednesday. Kansas City Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones (95) gestures to teh crowd during the third quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Kansas City Chiefs Reveal Major Chris Jones News on Wednesday On X, the Chiefs announced that the veteran star defensive tackle had won the AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. “Sack Nation stand up,” the post read. “Congrats, @StoneColdJones.” Jones put together a strong game against the New York Jets. In the 35-12 win for Kansas City, the 32-year-old defensive tackle racked up four total tackles, two sacks, and a defended pass. So far this season, the Chiefs have seen Jones total 17 tackles, 2.5 sacks, a fumble recovery, and three defended passes in eight games. Across his entire 163-game NFL career, all played for the Chiefs, Jones has totaled 356 tackles, 90 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, four fumble recoveries, two interceptions, a defensive touchdown, and 42 defended passes. Even though he may not be talked about nearly as much as the other main stars in Kansas City, he is one of the best in the NFL on the defensive line. Next up for the Chiefs will be a Week 10 matchup on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET on Sunday afternoon. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors have won eight straight games following their victory over the New Orleans Pelicans . The team is finding new ways to silence the media members who believed it wouldn't be as good this season, largely because of the organization's lack of significant moves during the offseason. There was plenty of buzz surrounding Golden State when the season began, as the Warriors were rumored to be pursuing some big names. Among those players were LeBron James and Anthony Davis. “The Golden State Warriors are planning a pursuit of LeBron James in free agency and Anthony Davis via trade this week, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, opening up the flexibility for such a possibility after Draymond Green declined his $27.6 million player option Monday morning," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. Next offseason could be an opportunity for Golden State to make some significant moves, as additional cap flexibility could become available. One name to keep an eye on is former Warrior and NBA champion Jordan Poole, who has made it clear that he would welcome a return in free agency. “We won a championship. So it works … to answer your question, definitely. This is my last year on the deal. I’m a free agent at the end of the season. So you never really know what’s going to happen,” Poole said. The shooting guard also mentioned that the Bay Area still feels like home to him. The two sides parted ways a few seasons ago when Golden State traded Poole to the Washington Wizards . “Several days after agreeing to send Bradley Beal to the Phoenix Suns in exchange for a package including Chris Paul, the Washington Wizards agreed to send the future Hall of Fame point guard to the Golden State Warriors Thursday for Jordan Poole, sources told ESPN's Adrian Wojnarowski,” ESPN’s Tim Bontemps wrote. Obviously, both sides have grown since 2023, and everything that happened back then is now in the past. Poole could be a good fit for Golden State, potentially providing an impact presence off the bench. After recently signing Brandin Podziemski to a contract extension, it is difficult to envision Poole returning as a starter. However, he could become a key piece of a strong second unit if a reunion happens. Why it could happen The Warriors could have some significant cap flexibility next offseason, especially if either Draymond Green or Jimmy Butler does not return. (Photo by Patrick Gorski/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Northwestern lost its first game in the new Ryan Field, and it happened without Aidan Chiles under center. Nicco Marchiol stepped in as the starter for the Wildcats, and played a solid game. The problem was that Iowa jumped out to a 14-0 lead early, and the ’Cats couldn’t claw their way back. The defensive struggles across the board, especially against the run, were exposed against Iowa, plus the Hawkeyes’ defense tore up the Wildcats’ offensive line and had Marchiol scrambling more than maybe anyone would have expected. Either way, Northwestern had a new quarterback this week so here’s a breakdown of that. Southpaw View Link There’s something that is so fascinating to me about watching a left-handed quarterback. While I’ve seen more lefties than normal with the absurd amount of college football I consume on a week-to-week basis (plus Michael Penix Jr. in the NFL), I’m still in the honeymoon phase of it. Marchiol’s longest completion of the game was just 22 yards — a massive difference compared to Chiles and his ability to stretch the field. However, Marchiol looked composed at quarterback, finishing 24-for-32 for 181 passing yards and a passing touchdown (I’ll get to the rushing later). Iowa’s defense is famous for limiting big plays, so even with Chiles, the game plan may have looked similar: a lot of shorter, underneath throws to move the ball. This first play starts out of the pistol. Marchiol fakes the handoff and waits for Iowa’s defenders to turn upfield before hitting Wilde on the outside curl route. Marchiol did stick with his first read this entire play, but he had a clean pocket and was able to wait for Wilde to break open. The second play is another play-action pass, this time out of the shotgun. Luke Dehnicke runs a 10-yard dig route across the middle, and Marchiol waits for him to cut before throwing right to his hands. Dehnicke gets some extra yardage on the play (this is the 22-yard gain), with Marchiol once again sticking to his first read to success. The third play is interesting. Marchiol gets the snap, takes a couple of steps to his right and then looks back to the left side of the field to find Dehnicke open on a drag route underneath. Marchiol ran a lot in this game, so the quarterback play-action design was something unique to see. The fourth play is a sprint rollout for Marchiol, who rolls to his left and gets it to Hayden Eligon II for a short gain. item.description: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images MLB rumors: Yankees targeting longtime Phillies star to fill gaping hole appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have reportedly identified Alec Bohm as a potential solution at third base following another early postseason exit. The Yankees were swept 3-0 by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series (ALDS) last month and are immediately looking to make upgrades. Per insider Jon Heyman, the Yankees are looking at the 30-year-old Bohm, who has spent all seven seasons of his MLB career with the Philadelphia Phillies. Philadelphia had the option of extending Bohm’s stay via a one-year contract projected to be around $23 million, but were unwilling to commit that kind of money. He is now projected to receive contracts in the $12-15 million annual range, with a number of teams actively monitoring the situation . Regardless, Ryan McMahon’s struggles at third base meant that New York’s third basemen combined for a .629 OPS in 2026, ranking 26th among MLB teams. McMahon hit .213 with 11 home runs and 41 RBIs in 124 regular-season games after arriving at the 2025 trade deadline. He batted .143 in the playoffs and has one year and $16 million remaining on his contract. Bohm has a career .273 batting average and .735 OPS with 85 home runs and a 17% strikeout rate compared with the MLB average of 22%. item.title: 2 Detroit Lions Will Almost Certainly Miss Germany Game
item.description: The Detroit Lions received some encouraging injury news Wednesday as they prepare for Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots in Germany. However, head coach Dan Campbell also revealed that two key starters remain unlikely to play. According to Wednesday’s update, Campbell said defensive end DJ Wonnum is expected to return to practice after missing Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins with a concussion. As long as Wonnum avoids any setbacks, Campbell believes he should be available against New England. Unfortunately, the news wasn’t nearly as promising for center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed. Neither player is expected to practice Wednesday, and Campbell indicated that both are doubtful at best for Sunday’s game. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) almost has his pass blocked by Detroit Lions edge rusher DJ Wonnum (98) that lead to an incomplete pass on the third down, during the first half of the N.F.L. game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Could Get DJ Wonnum Back Wonnum’s potential return would provide an important boost to Detroit’s defensive front. The veteran pass rusher was among five Lions ruled out against Miami , leaving Detroit shorthanded on defense. According to the Lions’ official November 6 injury report , Wonnum did not practice last week while dealing with his concussion. Wednesday’s expected return represents an encouraging development, although his availability remains dependent on avoiding setbacks and receiving the necessary clearance. Meanwhile, the outlook for Mays and Reed remains concerning. Both players were already expected to miss last Sunday’s game , and neither appears particularly close to returning. Mays continues to deal with an ankle injury, while Reed is recovering from a hip injury. According to the Lions’ official inactive report against Miami , veteran Juice Scruggs started at center in Mays’ absence, while Detroit relied on its secondary depth without Reed. The Lions will continue monitoring all three players throughout the week before making final decisions on their availability. For now, Wonnum appears to be trending in the right direction, while Mays and Reed face an uphill battle to suit up against the Patriots.

item.title: Why Jake Paul’s $150 million boxing career could be over way faster than you might think
item.description: Why Jake Paul’s $150 million boxing career could be over way faster than you might think originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jake Paul has made it a career out of saying outlandish things. The YouTuber-turned-boxer is really doubling down on a promise he made before his fight against Cedric Doumbe. Paul faces Doumbe on Christmas Eve in Dubai. It’s the first bout for “The Problem Child” since getting knocked out by Anthony Joshua last December. Before the Joshua loss, Paul (12-2) was on a six-fight win streak. He has seven knockout wins. Paul faces someone in Doumbe with 45 knockout wins in kickboxing. In his short MMA career, Doumbe has six knockout wins. Though this is his first boxing fight since 2015, Doumbe is one of the most dangerous athletes in combat sports. Paul understands this, and said he would put his career on the line in this fight. "If he wins, I will hang up the gloves and call it a day," Paul said on his YouTube channel via ESPN . "But if he loses, the man who calls himself 'The Best' just got beat up by a YouTuber with a titanium jaw." It was unknown if Paul would fight again after suffering a broken jaw against Joshua. After reportedly earning $92 million for the fight, he contemplated retiring after multiple surgeries to fix it. Many expect Paul to go back on his word. However, during a press conference in Paris, Paul doubled down on his retirement claims. “100% retiring if I lose to this guy. Sure, like 100%. For sure. For sure, for sure,” Paul said. Jake Paul career earnings According to CelebrityNetWorth , Paul has a net worth of $200 million. His biggest payday before the Joshua fight was against Mike Tyson, where Paul reportedly came away with $40 million. Before that, in fights against Nate Diaz, Mike Perry, and others, Paul was earning between $2 to $7 million. item.title: Luis de la Fuente hits out at ‘lies’ about Lamine Yamal injury after Barcelona star misses Czechia game
item.description: SPLIT, CROATIA - OCTOBER 06: Lamine Yamal of Spain looks on during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Croatia and Spain at Stadion Poljud on October 06, 2026 in Split, Croatia. (Photo by Francesco Scaccianoce - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Spain boss Luis de la Fuente confirmed Lamine Yama l will join up with the squad later this week at a press conference and then hit out at some of the talk surrounding the Barcelona star’s current situation. Yamal will miss Thursday’s Nations League fixture against Czechia due to a knee injury, but there’s been talk in the media that the teenager is receiving special treatment. A debate on Cadena SER this week claimed Yamal’s absence was sending a message that the forward “can do whatever he wants” and that he’s a “special case.” De la Fuente was asked if he was angry about such talk and snapped out a pretty forceful message. “What hurts me the most is the lying, the lack of rigor, the lack of truthfulness, and the fabrication,” he told a news conference. “That’s why I’ve revealed more than I should have, but it’s the only way for people to know the truth. I can’t stand people who try to deceive you and lie. “I’m not worried. I’m here to clear things up. He doesn’t have any special privileges. We would have done the same with anyone. It doesn’t bother anyone. We miss everyone who isn’t with us. That’s football, injuries.” Yamal is progressing well from his knee discomfort and is expected to join the national team on Friday.

item.title: Skip Bayless says Carson Wentz ‘can’t play football’ after Vikings performance vs Bills
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Carson Wentz’s performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the quarterback. The 33-year-old threw for 81 yards and completed only 8 passes out of 25 attempts, which meant he had a completion rate of only 32%. Wentz ended up with a passer rating of 8.9, which is the lowest for any player with 25 or more passes in the NFL since 2019. His inability to get the ball to the end zone led the Vikings to suffer a 6-23 defeat and pushed them out of the top place in the NFC North. This was Wentz’s chance to prove that he could take over Kyler Murray as the starter, but he put on a horrific performance, which led to the Vikings deciding to trade for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, which was just a day after the game. Skip Bayless believes Carson Wentz is not accurate consistently Wentz was a regular starter in the league for 7 seasons. He was a second pick in the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles; however, he was never able to fulfil the promise he showed at North Dakota State. In the games he has started, Wentz has thrown for over 23,000 yards and completed 62.7% of his passes. But none of that impressed Bayless, who fired shots at Wentz, discussing his performance on Monday Night Football. “I have been hard on him. I was hard on Carson Wentz coming out of college before he got drafted. I didn’t like him at North Dakota State. I didn’t like his poise or his feel. He’s one of those guys who’s the prototype 6’5, 240-pound, rocket-arm quarterback who can’t play football, and he’s not accurate consistently. All he can do is throw it through a brick wall. Well, that’s not how you win NFL games at the highest level,” said Bayless on Gridiron. With Cousins now set to take over the reins as the starting quarterback, Wentz’s future with the Vikings could be questionable. They already have Kyler Murray, who can play as the backup. He is definitely a good piece to have on a team, as he has proven experience starting games, which not a lot of backups in the league have. However, after his performance against the Bills, fans would definitely not be happy if they see him take snaps under center. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Are the Wizards Asking Too Much of Kyshawn George?
item.description: The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become. Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wizards, but his recent performances have also raised questions about whether the Wizards are putting too much responsibility on him too soon. George has shown that he can help this team in several areas of the game. The 6-foot-7 forward has become a key piece of the Wizards’ offense, using his scoring ability and creative playmaking to make opportunities for himself and his teammates. Over the last few games, George has become particularly encouraging. George scored 22 points against the Orlando Magic on Nov. 2, followed by 25 points facing the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 4. He then dropped 33 points in another loss to Atlanta the next game, adding eight assists and five three-pointers. Those numbers show why Washington has continued to give George opportunities with the ball in his hands. However, his development isn’t just about scoring and how many points he can score. The Wizards also need to find the right role for him as he continues to improve in the NBA. He’s been able to score, defend multiple positions, and help create offense for his teammates. Washington has also been experimenting with using him as a point guard when Trae Young is not playing. That responsibility has not always been easy. George recorded eight turnovers against the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 23, a performance that showed some of the challenges of asking him to run the Wizards’ offense. He has the ability to make plays, but becoming a good ball handler takes time. After George’s 22-point performance on the Chicago Bulls defense on Oct. 24, Wizards coach Brian Keefe discussed his ability to create more opportunities by getting into the paint. “You saw him being able to create and get into the paint,” Keefe said. “A lot more paint touches for us tonight, which we wanted to emphasize, and he was a catalyst for that.” The comments, reported by Roundtable Sports , show that Washington finds value in what George can bring when he is attacking the basket instead of forcing himself to make all of the plays. item.description: Jonathan Hui-Imagn Images NFL rumors: Rams called Chargers about Ladd McConkey trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams reportedly expressed interest in acquiring wide receiver Ladd McConkey from the Los Angeles Chargers ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline but were turned down by their crosstown rivals. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano revealed Wednesday that the Rams were believed to be the team that contacted the Chargers about McConkey, who remained with the organization despite its winless start to the 2026 season. “Fowler: The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry. Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call. Overall, though, the Rams didn’t seriously consider a receiver move because they expect both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to return this season. And in the short term, they believe Matthew Stafford can maximize the supporting cast of receivers.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Rams entered the deadline seeking potential reinforcements after injuries sidelined Nacua and Adams , leaving quarterback Matthew Stafford without his top two receiving options. Despite the reported inquiry, Los Angeles ultimately remained inactive on the trade market. Chargers retain Ladd McConkey despite winless start to 2026 season Image Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images McConkey has recorded 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown across six appearances this season, averaging 16.8 yards per reception. The 24-year-old delivered one of his strongest performances against the Rams in Week 8, catching four passes for 86 yards, including a season-long 54-yard reception, during the Chargers’ 24-9 loss . His production has been inconsistent amid the Chargers’ struggles, but he remains one of their most important offensive weapons. The Chargers have opened the season with eight consecutive losses, falling to 0-8 following Sunday’s 44-22 defeat against the Houston Texans . Despite their disappointing record, the organization declined to move McConkey, who recorded 82 receptions for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns during his rookie campaign in 2024. Meanwhile, the Rams have won three consecutive games to improve to 5-4 following Sunday’s 20-13 victory over the Washington Commanders . item.title: Eugenio Chacarra targets Race to Dubai glory as Rory McIlroy pushes
item.description: Eugenio Chacarra is aiming to bring his finest golf to hold off Rory McIlroy and claim the Race to Dubai crown at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship . The Spaniard holds a 533.93-point advantage over Masters champion McIlroy entering the final event at Jumeirah Golf Estates, where 2,000 points are up for grabs for the winner. On the back of a third-place finish at last week’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, McIlroy is targeting a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title, a triumph that would match Colin Montgomerie’s record tally of eight overall. Meanwhile, the likes of Patrick Reed , USPGA champion Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm and Open winner Ryan Fox retain a mathematical possibility of making a late charge for top spot should the frontrunners falter. Mcllroy will be hoping to secure fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title (Getty) Chacarra recognises there is minimal margin for error as he prepares to head out on Thursday in the marquee final pairing alongside McIlroy. "Obviously we know how good Rory McIlroy is and he is one of my idols. It is going to be a tough test and that is what I dreamed of since I was little," Chacarra said at a pre-tournament press conference on Wednesday. "But I already beat him in India (at the DP World India Championship in October), so I need to remind myself that I can compete with him and I can beat him like I did already a couple weeks ago. "This is a course that he has had a lot of success (on) and I only played once and didn’t do very good, but they are just numbers. This is golf and crazy things happen. "I am just going to enjoy myself, and if I bring my A-game, I am going to be able to compete with him on Sunday."

item.title: Marcus Rashford races to be fit for Liverpool trip as Man Utd put new recovery programme in place for his groin problem
item.description: Manchester United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are hopeful Marcus Rashford will be fit for their trip to Liverpool a week on Sunday after the forward began a new treatment programme on a groin problem. The 29-year-old has missed United's last six games, but a visit to a specialist in Dublin has given the club fresh optimism ahead of a clash against the rivals he has so often hurt. Specialist visit sparks fresh hope Manchester United hope Rashford will be available for their next game at Liverpool a week on Sunday after he started a new recovery programme, according to the Daily Mail . The forward travelled to Dublin last week with a member of the club's medical staff to see a groin specialist, and a fresh plan is now in place. Rashford picked up a hip injury at the World Cup before returning to Old Trafford in the summer following a season on loan at Barcelona. He has since missed United's last six games after the problem was aggravated and spread to his groin. Rashford offered to play through the pain Rashford featured in the first six league games of the season, as well as the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton and the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in mid-October. He is said to have a good relationship with Michael Carrick and wanted to support the head coach during a difficult spell. However, playing while carrying the injury only made it worse. item.description: Shrewsbury Town are 15th in League Two [Getty Images] Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit. Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control. "Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview. "So we looked in Turkey, Poland, Portugal and Holland but the clubs we were looking at, something didn't align for one reason or another and a lot of it came down to did we think our group can help the football club because we want to bring the town firmly behind the club." Wycherley first announced his plans to find a successor five years ago and Friedel says with Davidson already being a majority shareholder of Edinburgh-based The Spartans in Scottish League Two, they wanted a club they could take forward both on and off the field. "The one-town club really appealed to us because we want to intergrate the club even more into the town than it is now and when you look at the investment going into the EFL, the foreign investment going into it, there's a reason for it because there's no better place for football than the United Kingdom.
